newsitem.title: RUSSIA: August holidays slow Russia's air cargo market.
newsitem.headline: August holidays slow Russia's air cargo market.

text.p: The peak holiday season made Russia's air cargo market less stable during last three weeks, compared with the previous three weeks, but rates had changed little, a Reuters survey showed.
Igor Mordvinov, senior sales manager of Burlington Air Express Moscow, said clients made fewer orders to carry cargo then usual for this time of year.
"But we see that the market will be more active in the second part of August and it will grow more from September," he said.

Mordvinov said that rates had not changed during last three weeks, in spite of the market slackness, but Air France's cargo sales manager in Moscow Ouabed Khaled said that his company had increased its rates.
He gave no further details, but said last week Air France had increased export shipments from Sheremetyevo.
"Clients in the market look for quality of service and do not mention the rates level," he said, adding that business "is going very well".
An forwarder who asked not to be named said that Air France sent about 60 tonnes of cargo in July from Moscow compared with around 15-20 tonnes in previous months this year.

Ilya Maslennikov, senior cargo manager at the newly-established forwarding firm of MBB Trans, agent for Aeroflot, Delta Air Lines, Lufthansa and Russia's Transaero, said that the market was thin since the begining of August and may stabilise only next month.
He also said activity at Sheremetyevo airport was low due to high handling rates and "unrealisable" customs rules.
"Many Sheremetyevo-based forwarders were obliged to cut operations there and went out of business," he said.
He said many clients preferred to send cargo from the United States to Finland by sea and then load the cargo on to trucks to deliver it to Moscow, avoiding Sheremetyevo airport customs.

Nikolai Belyaev, senior cargo manager at EMS Garant Post, cargo agent for Air France, said that his company saw a 30-40 percent fall in cargo volume during the last three weeks compared with the last few months.
"It is normal for August when many clients often took a break," he said.
Belyaev said that shipments of periodicals were stable in August while others cargo's volumes fell.
Peter Vins, president of Vinlund company, said that export shipments were normal during the last three weeks.
"We had a very small fall in cargo volumes this month," he said, but added that September may be more active compared with August. "People will come back to work and new contracts come."
Vins said there were many shipments between U.S. destinations and Moscow in the last three weeks.

Burlington's Mordvinov said his company was ready to carry heavy machinery cargo from Central Russia to India. "Destinations between the United States, Europe and Russia were less active then usual for us," he added.
Mordvinov also said that Burlington Air Express Moscow made a few sucsesfull sea shipment operations with heavy cargo from St Petersburg.
"It is a promising business and we will develop it," he added.

Maslennikov said there had been varied cargo imports from South-East Asia to Russia during the last three weeks, including electronics, telecommunication equipment and clothes. - Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520 - www.racs.com
